title: A Big Storm Called Isaias Is Heading for the U.S. Gulf Coast
summary:
A tropical storm named Isaias formed on Wednesday in warm ocean water near eastern Mexico. Forecasters think it will quickly get stronger and become a hurricane. It is expected to reach the U.S. Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday, but its path could still change.

Michael Brennan leads the U.S. National Hurricane Center. He said Isaias could become a major Category 3 hurricane, which means very strong winds. Forecasters also warned about ocean water being pushed onto land and heavy rain that could cause flooding near the coast.

People are getting ready. The governors of Florida and Alabama declared emergencies for dozens of counties. A big shrimp festival in Gulf Shores, Alabama, was canceled. A college football game between Georgia and Alabama on Saturday might also be affected.

This hurricane season has been unusually quiet. If Isaias becomes a hurricane, it could tie or break a record from 1905 for the latest first hurricane of the Atlantic season.
why_it_matters: Knowing a storm is coming helps families make a plan, pack supplies and stay safe.
